summary: No high/critical findings. The exact-match dict lookup in _resolve_source_name fails-closed on all tested spoofing vectors (@-userinfo, IDN, percent-encoded dot, subdomain suffix, port injection). Warning log prints only public URL strings; no secrets leak. _resolve_source_name is exception-safe.
owasp_categories_reviewed: A01 Broken Access Control (N/A — no auth decisions)
A03 Injection (URL parsing — stdlib urlparse, no string-concat SQL/HTML)
A04 Insecure Design (source_name = internal vocabulary, no trust decision)
A05 Security Misconfiguration (N/A — no config change)
A08 Software & Data Integrity (FeedParserDict normalisation prevents non-JSON values from leaking into pending_articles JSON columns — defence-in-depth)
A09 Logging Failures (warning format reviewed — no secret leak)
A10 SSRF (feed URLs come from operator-controlled feeds.json; load_feeds already validates http/https scheme at news_bot.py:137)

log_leak_analysis.warning_log_contents: Unknown netloc for RSS entry: link={link!r} feed={url!r}
log_leak_analysis.secret_risk: None. `link` and `url` are public RSS URLs from feedparser / operator-controlled feeds.json. Project-wide pattern: regular logger.warning output is NOT routed through sanitize_error_message (Decision 11 scopes sanitisation to last_error storage + admin-chat). Introducing sanitisation only here would be inconsistent; not a Task 5 concern.

malformed_url_handling.behaviour: _resolve_source_name wraps urlparse in try/except and handles None/empty via `link or ''`. Returns 'other' on any failure. Verified by tests: test_resolve_source_name_empty_string + test_resolve_source_name_no_scheme.

dependencies_added: None. Uses only stdlib urllib.parse.urlparse and existing project functions.
